terms.definition: An installable unit with a plugin.json: its pages, sections, settings and declarations.
A native program of one domain with a sidecar.json that plugin pages talk to.

The file that sok plugin pack or sok sidecar release writes and that a registry lists: <id>-<version>.tgz of a plugin, <file name>-<version>-<platform>.tar.gz of a sidecar, or soksak-<version>-<platform>-<host>.zip of an application bundle.
The folder that plugins/installed.json records for an installed plugin.
A document of a plugin that a document region shows at soksak://<plugin id>/<path>.
A native region of a surface that shows the transfer images of a sidecar (docs/spec/native-surfaces.md).
The acknowledged removal of one image generation's render ownership and configuration while retaining its surface session (docs/spec/sidecars.md#image-envelope).
An address soksak://<owner>/<command> that opens from outside the application.
The file logs/application.log under the configuration directory: the host lines, the page lines sent through report, and the standard error of the sidecars that the host starts.
The events page.trace.*, host.trace.*, host.sampler.* and sidecar trace events that the layers store in the event files under logs/ while the setting diagnostics.performance is on.
A file logs/state-<time>.json that the debug view writes: the state of the host, the versions and every window at one time.
The dialog that Help > Debug opens: it records a state file, lists the files of logs/ and saves them.
One record of the contract in docs/spec/logging.md: a JSON object with a time, a sequence number, a level, a layer, a declared name and fields.
The declared kind of an event (lifecycle, input, call, io, frame) that decides how the writer stores it.
One kind of data of a document region, its elements or its requests, that the host collects only while a page subscribes to it (docs/spec/native-surfaces.md#document-streams).
The elements of a document region at one point, sent as {seq, nodes, total, truncated} under acknowledgement of its seq.
The identifier that one native input receives from the layer that first sees it and that every later layer carries (cids in an event).

The rules by language that list each source of occurrences (an empty catch, a discarded result, a goroutine, a registered observer, an error return) and require an event in its function or a reason marker.
The one comment form (default|silent): <reason> that states why a source of occurrences stores no event.
Rebuilding the screen of a session from its stored inputs with the replay executable of its sidecar, to compare the stored hashes of the screens (docs/spec/replay.md).
The events of the layer sidecar that one run (boot) of a sidecar produced for one session; its sequence restarts at 1, and a replay compares each segment on its own (docs/spec/replay.md#segments).
The SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of a screen, a grid of cells with a cursor, that docs/spec/replay.md defines; a sidecar and a page store it per frame record.
The diagnostic nonce and source generation, raster, and sequence encoded in a visible QR code to correlate a captured image with its exact source raster.

An explicitly started diagnostic fixed overlay with a transparent background and a unique opaque border whose captured pixels identify the visual viewport edges without changing document layout or input.

A provider-defined runtime grid coordinate used to place an input caret in a raster presentation overlay; it is distinct from the engine cursor and is not part of the generic screen hash or replay inputs.
The data a release ships for one stored file when its format number rises: from, to and an ordered list of named operations.
The oldest stored format a definition chain migrates; an older form is refused.
A stored-format change that moves folders or crosses files: it has no definition, its release documents it and reinstalling carries it out.
The kind of a stored file of a configuration folder or a project root: numbered, transient, log, external or fetched.
The core operation of the memory saver that releases the surface of a hidden tab that stays in the layout; the tab keeps its reports and the state its plugin wrote.
The core operation of the memory saver that mounts an unloaded tab again from the state its plugin wrote when the tab is shown.
A reason of the memory saver that keeps a tab from being unloaded, such as shown, keep:modified or media.
The core function, turned on and off by the setting memorySaver, that unloads hidden tabs after a delay and under memory pressure and restores them when they are shown.

A separate web view of a plugin on its soksak://<plugin id> origin, with one view per tab, that runs plugin code the declared UI vocabulary cannot express (free DOM, text input with an input method, a canvas or editor, or a document region or image region).
The object {sidebar, section, key, path?, role?} that a request uses to address one control of a declared section (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).
One sidebar as core.sidebars reports it, identified by left, right, or cardId:side.

A sidebar section whose every element is one of list, tree, button or status-line, which the workbench draws from the declared UI snapshots and pull replies that a plugin sends (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).
The message that carries one declared UI value of one status, pushed by the plugin with {plugin, status, seq, value, skipped} and acknowledged by seq.
One node of a declared UI value: a list, tree, button or status-line, or an item or node of a list or tree (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).
The declared element that shows one line of plain text in a declared UI value (docs/spec/declared-ui.md). It is not the status line that ends a window sidebar.
The schema of the value of a declared UI status, which the plugin declares in exposes.status and the receiver validates with the rules of docs/spec/declared-ui.md.
A status that a sidebar section names with the `status` form of its declaration, whose value is a declared UI value (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).
A tree node with a nonempty children array or `branch: true`, which the workbench draws with an expand control (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).
A tree node with `branch: true` and no child nodes in the current value; it has an expand control while its children are absent (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).
A sidebar section declared with the `status` form, whose body the workbench draws from a declared UI status (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).
The value of a declared UI status: an object with the field `elements` that a declared UI snapshot or pull reply carries (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).
The response of a pull of a declared UI status: {seq, value}, where value is the source's current value and is null when the source has no value yet (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).
The pair of a process and its registration of a declared UI status (docs/spec/declared-ui.md).

A plugin's override of the content of a fixed window sidebar, which applies only while the focused card's active surface is that plugin's (docs/spec/external-sidebars.md, Override context and rail border).
The mark of a status whose value changed while its snapshot was in transit; the acknowledgement of that snapshot sends the latest value of the status and clears the mark.
A process of a plugin, with a platform web view attached to the window, that runs DOM-free logic which neither a view nor a sidecar can hold; it exists only when the contract requires it.
A call across a process boundary from its start until it receives its reply or ends with a timeout, a lost peer or a failure; the core status core.plugin.open-calls counts the open calls of a plugin.
The createCalls module of plugin-api that sends a call over a transport, resolves or rejects it by its reply, and reports its timeouts, lost peers, late replies and open calls.
A count of a loss, a skipped value, a late reply or a presentation abandoned, kept in the core status core.plugin.losses per plugin until the application ends; it is not a log event in a release.
A surface placed in a card that a `button` in the sidebar opens when the plugin that declares it needs a view.
The wait of a window commit for a view to present its content after a card layout change.
The table that a view registers with its host, holding each workbench shortcut and its owner.
The fields of a call: its id, command and cancellation; a reply carries the same id.
The reserved host `core` on the soksak:// scheme, which serves the view import map targets, the shared modules and the modules of granted items to views, and which no plugin id can use.
The module `@soksak/plugin-api/view` that a view page imports, which exports the view side of the call layer and of the declared UI snapshots over the view channel.

The import map of a view page, with the five entries `soksak`, `@soksak/plugin-api`, `@soksak/plugin-api/view`, `@soksak/plugin-api/screen-hash` and `@soksak/shared/`, which map to their `soksak://core` addresses.

A contribution of a plugin to an extension point of another installed plugin, whose provider is installed and enabled, whose range contains the version of the point, and whose entry matches the schema of the point.
A contribution item whose provider is installed and enabled and whose range contains the version of the point, used only by the core root grant.
The document-start script and the message handler `sok-view` that the host registers with a view's web view configuration, through which a view page sends and receives its calls and snapshots.

The web view configuration that the host creates for one view, with `isView`, the plugin id of the surface, the document-start scripts of the view channel and of the theme, and the handler `sok-view`.
The document of a view whose ready message the host has recorded, the only document that receives host messages.
The file plugins/installed.json, which maps each plugin id to its recorded path.
The key that identifies the owner of an exposure registration.
A declared UI snapshot that is sent for one status and not yet acknowledged.
The name field of a plugin's package.json. The installation record does not hold it.

The bytes that a document region keeps for its plugin under binary ids, from an upload until a download or a native take releases each id, or until the region closes (docs/spec/native-surfaces.md#document-regions).
The 32-character lowercase hexadecimal id that the host mints for one stored upload of a document region's binary store.
The value that the host page of a plugin saves through its channel and that the host keeps for the next start of the page (docs/spec/plugin-host.md).

The control that keyboard focus moves to for a declared tree node: its label control when that control exists and is enabled, otherwise the expand control of a branch (docs/spec/declared-ui.md, Tree keys).
An independent ordinary AppKit text view in an application window that diagnostic activation checks compare with the same native keys.
